title: Fever
hpi_narrative: {{patient_name}} presents with acute onset high fever, severe sore throat, drooling, muffled 'hot potato' voice, stridor, and tripod positioning (leaning forward, chin thrust out). Epiglottitis is a life-threatening airway emergency. Historically caused by H. influenzae type B (now rare due to Hib vaccine) — now more commonly Group A Strep, S. pneumoniae, Staph. Do NOT examine the throat or agitate the child — can trigger complete airway obstruction! Let the child remain in position of comfort. Immediate management: keep child calm, avoid invasive exam, arrange for controlled airway management in OR by anesthesia/ENT (awake fiberoptic intubation). Croup (laryngotracheitis) is viral, slower onset, barky cough — epiglottitis is rapid, toxic-appearing, no cough. Lateral neck X-ray shows 'thumbprint sign' (swollen epiglottis) but do NOT send child to radiology unattended. Treatment: IV antibiotics (ceftriaxone + vancomycin), steroids (dexamethasone).
